findings.title: Non-2xx verifier responses now masked as "unavailable" and body discarded
findings.desc: Any non-OK reply from the verifier (e.g. 400 for oversized/malformed `leanCode`, or a verifier that signals compile failure with a non-200 status) is reported as `unavailable: true` with only `HTTP <status>`, so real verification failures and request errors are silently presented as "verifier offline" and the verifier's error payload (previously forwarded) is lost.

findings.title: Offline banner text wrong for the `verifier-error` reason
findings.desc: The banner unconditionally claims the verifier "is not configured or unreachable" and tells the user to set `LEAN_VERIFIER_URL`, which is inaccurate/misleading when the route returned `reason: "verifier-error"` (URL configured, verifier reachable but erroring).

findings.title: `reason`/`detail` from the route are never surfaced
findings.desc: The route carefully distinguishes `verifier-not-configured` / `verifier-unreachable` / `verifier-error` (plus `detail`), but `verifyLean` drops both fields, so no caller can differentiate or display the cause; either propagate them or drop them from the response.

FINDINGS:
1. app/api/verification/lean/route.ts:45-49 | Medium | correctness | Non-2xx verifier responses now masked as "unavailable" and body discarded | Any non-OK reply from the verifier (e.g. 400 for oversized/malformed `leanCode`, or a verifier that signals compile failure with a non-200 status) is reported as `unavailable: true` with only `HTTP <status>`, so real verification failures and request errors are silently presented as "verifier offline" and the verifier's error payload (previously forwarded) is lost.
2. app/components/features/lean-display/LeanCodeDisplay.tsx:131-143 | Low | misleading docs/UI | Offline banner text wrong for the `verifier-error` reason | The banner unconditionally claims the verifier "is not configured or unreachable" and tells the user to set `LEAN_VERIFIER_URL`, which is inaccurate/misleading when the route returned `reason: "verifier-error"` (URL configured, verifier reachable but erroring).
3. app/lib/formalization/api.ts:118-130 | Low | API/consistency drift | `reason`/`detail` from the route are never surfaced | The route carefully distinguishes `verifier-not-configured` / `verifier-unreachable` / `verifier-error` (plus `detail`), but `verifyLean` drops both fields, so no caller can differentiate or display the cause; either propagate them or drop them from the response.

findings.title: Verifier HTTP error responses are swallowed and reported as "unavailable"
findings.desc: Any non-2xx from the verifier (including a 4xx that rejects the submitted Lean code, or a 5xx that carries `errors` in the body) is now reported as `unavailable: true` with the body discarded, so a genuinely failing/rejected proof is presented to the user as "not checked" and all diagnostic output is lost.

findings.title: Route's `reason`/`detail` fields are never consumed
findings.desc: The route returns a structured `reason` ("verifier-not-configured" | "verifier-unreachable" | "verifier-error") plus `detail`, but `verifyLean` drops both, so the UI can only show a hedged "not configured or unreachable" message and no debugging detail reaches the client — either propagate the fields or stop emitting them.

findings.title: Failures of the app's own API route still surface as "Verification Failed"
findings.desc: `verifyLean` never checks `res.ok`, so a 400 ("leanCode is required") or a 500/non-JSON response from `/api/verification/lean` yields `unavailable: false, valid: false` (or a thrown error caught as `invalid`), i.e. an unchecked proof is again labeled as a failed proof — the exact confusion this change targets.

findings.title: Prior real verification errors are discarded when the verifier drops out mid-retry
findings.desc: If attempts 1–2 produced genuine `errors` and attempt 3 hits an unavailable verifier, the loop returns `errors: ""` and calls `onErrors("")`, so known-bad proof diagnostics are wiped and the UI reports "proof not checked" rather than the failures already observed.

findings.title: Verifier error responses are swallowed, losing real diagnostics
findings.desc: Any non-2xx from the verifier (including 4xx like "leanCode too large" or a genuine build-service rejection) is now reported as `unavailable` with only `HTTP <status>`; the verifier's error body is discarded, so users see "Verifier offline" and an invitation to set `LEAN_VERIFIER_URL` even though the verifier is configured and reachable, and no actionable error text reaches the UI.

findings.title: Banner text contradicts some unavailable reasons
findings.desc: The banner asserts the verifier "is not configured or unreachable" and tells the user to set `LEAN_VERIFIER_URL`, but the same status is produced for `verifier-error` (configured, reachable, returned HTTP error), making the guidance wrong in that case.

findings.title: `reason`/`detail` from the route are never consumed
findings.desc: The route carefully distinguishes `verifier-not-configured` / `verifier-unreachable` / `verifier-error` and adds a `detail`, but `verifyLean` drops both fields, so the distinction is dead weight and the UI cannot show which failure occurred.
